chapter: Cavalcade, Wynonie Harris and the 1953 show
title: Wynonie Harris's stage act and records
summary: Harris was hard to get along with and wanted to be the whole show; Durham controlled the band and arranged Bloodshot Eyes and All She Wants to Do Is Rock.

story.theme_name: Singers and the musicians who accompanied them
story.community_name: Working with Sinatra: bands, Vegas and the Sands

blocks.x: Well, now, tell me about WYNONIE HARRIS, what kind of guy was he?
He was hard to get along with. Nobody could get along with him.
Why was that?
(Inaudible.) They'd do what I say to do.
Was it really that _______?
Yeah. So he didn't like the bands to play on the stage. He wanted to do the whole show.
Oh, he'd like you down in the pit or something.

Yeah, we used to start off with the grooves, rocking the blues. (Inaudible.) But he didn't understand, and I told him, the people that are setting in this audience, they (inaudible). So, finally, when they'd get offstage I'd play the blues with the band. (Inaudible) you got some band. (Inaudible.) So that's the way I got the show going.
I had to watch him, though, because he'd get around the sound system and (inaudible).
Did you say too that he had to get out on the floor amongst the people?
(Inaudible.)
Yeah.

Sometimes he had an introduction (inaudible). So that's the way we made novelties out of that. (Inaudible.) He'd make the introduction. (Inaudible.) And he wouldn't show up, they'd make it again. (Inaudible ) he walked in front of the theater, you know, and -- boom, stick his foot out. The guy would put the light on him.

So that all got to be an act, so whenever he was in -- we'd stand in the bar for the introduction because he knew how to put on this show. I may be all down in the audience by the time he get there (inaudible) still making them introductions. People would go crazy. And that's the way he got it going.
So he got so he wouldn't work with anybody, and that's how I got the band, see. Then I could control it.
Well, he did -- he had a lot of hit records, didn't he?
Yeah. I made that Bloodshot Eyes with him, and All's You Want To Do Is Rock and all those things.
Oh, you made those with him?
Yeah.
Well, were they written arrangements for those?
Yeah, they were written arrangements.
Oh.
Oh, yeah.
Well, how many things did you do with him? I mean, did you do quite a few sessions?
Not too many sessions.
No.

No, we just did the last few things he had. The rest of it he had done. But I had to show him, so that show was really going over. Back in New York, they said, man, they got 5,000 or 6,000 tonight and all blues, don't want to hear not -- (inaudible) same key, same tempo, (inaudible) the girl, right after her and then Larry with the band come on, (inaudible).
